name: SIGINT
standfirst: Security research and practitioner news, scored for novelty and actionability.
colophon: sigint.wtf — the correct response to most of these CVEs. Scored by machine against a hand-written rubric; ranking is opinion, not fact.

items.title: Nudge the Judge: Uncovering Program Decision Hijacking in Real-World Jev Applications
items.dek: JevProbe detects program decision hijacking in LLM-as-judge applications: 81.5% of 228 apps exhibit exploitable decision flips.
items.unproven: Evaluated on public GitHub applications; does not establish exploitation feasibility under production guardrails or demonstrate impact on enterprise agent deployments entering the reader's SDLC.

items.title: X.js: A Live Benchmark for Node.js Taint-Style Vulnerabilities
items.dek: X.js: live benchmark of 1,159 validated Node.js taint-style exploits across code injection, prototype pollution, and path traversal.
items.unproven: Coverage is JavaScript/npm only; does not cover polyglot dependency chains or transitive supply-chain risk in the reader's financial services environment.

items.title: Towards Safe Autonomy for Computer Use
items.dek: Dual-LLM framework derives deterministic trust boundaries for computer-use agents, separating trusted and untrusted screen regions without confirmation fatigue.
items.unproven: tested on limited agent implementations; does not address agents with custom tool integration outside accessibility tree coverage

items.title: Kairos: Transactional Security Enforcement at the System Boundary for LLM Agents
items.dek: Reference monitor at agent isolation boundary enforces transactional rollback of tool calls, shell commands, and writes based on source trust.
items.unproven: prototype implementation; does not measure overhead or test against agents with side-channel access or exfiltration via timing

items.title: CVE-2026-104935 — Ivanti Connect Secure Authentication Bypass by Spoofing Vulnerability
items.dek: Ivanti Connect Secure. Confirmed exploited in the wild. Federal remediation due 16 October.

items.title: CVE-2026-96951 — Microsoft Windows Command Injection Vulnerability
items.dek: Microsoft Windows. Confirmed exploited in the wild. Federal remediation due 16 October.

items.title: VulnBump: A Benchmark for Fixing Vulnerable Dependencies in Real Projects While Keeping the Build and Tests Green
items.dek: VulnBump benchmark: 307 real-world dependency upgrades show Snyk's Evo Remediation Agent passes 90.2% vs. baseline 46.9%, Claude Code 59.6%.
items.unproven: whether agent performance holds on unreleased vulnerabilities or zero-days; applicability to private package registries or proprietary build systems

items.title: AegisAsync: Symbolic Async-Event Simulation for Risks in Python Asynchronous Programs
items.dek: Bytecode-based detector for Python async event-ordering bugs finds 457 confirmed bugs in 2,500 PyPI packages with 50% precision.
items.unproven: Does not establish whether detected bugs represent exploitable security flaws or denial-of-service risks; detection precision drops to 3.2% on a sample of real flake8-async findings.

items.title: Pin It on Anyone: Certified Targeted Displacement of Multi-Bit LLM Watermarks Without the Key
items.dek: Attack on multi-bit LLM watermarks allows framing of output to arbitrary accounts without the secret key.
items.unproven: tested on five watermarking methods and four models; does not establish whether watermarks are deployment standard or whether the reader's agents use them

items.title: Discovery or Memorization? A Faithful Benchmark for Real-World Business-Logic Vulnerability Discovery
items.dek: AnonVul benchmark of 132 business-logic vulnerabilities across nine languages tests whether agents discover real flaws or memorize training data.
items.unproven: whether current frontier models saturate the benchmark within one release cycle; generalization beyond the 43 languages and vulnerability patterns included

items.title: Zod 4.6.6 compromised by malware?
items.dek: Zod npm package 4.6.6 hit by supply-chain malware; evidence of active compromise in transit dependency.
items.unproven: scope and exploit chain of malware payload not detailed; no confirmation of how many installs received infected version

items.title: Show HN: Parsimony – an open-source benchmark for how much code AI models add
items.dek: Parsimony benchmark measures coding units added by AI models across existing SWE-bench patches; informs model selection when integrating code generation into SDLC.
items.unproven: whether metric predicts long-term maintenance burden in production codebases or correlates with security debt

items.title: ARACDE: Retrofitting Databases with ABAC using External Authorization Engines
items.authors: Karthikeya S M Yelisetty et al.
items.dek: ARCADE externalizes database access control to Cedar policy engine for MySQL and PostgreSQL with minimal code changes.
items.unproven: Demonstrated on two databases; does not establish whether policy composition methodology scales to large multi-tenant deployments or covers all SDLC threat models the reader defends against.

items.title: DPOison-VL: Clean Preference Poisoning in Vision-Language Direct Preference Optimization
items.dek: Clean preference poisoning attack on vision-language model DPO training uses imperceptible image perturbations; achieves 98% attack success.
items.unproven: Limited to DPO alignment; does not establish whether attack persists post-deployment or applies to agents in SDLC pipeline the reader oversees.

items.title: Encrypted Skills Can Become New Security Exploits If AI Agents Know How to Decipher
items.dek: Ciphered skill injection embeds encoded malicious instructions in third-party agent skills; scanners rarely detect them.
items.unproven: limited to eight models and 139 test pairs; does not measure detection rates of production skill scanners or describe realistic skill repositories

items.title: Standing, Not Truth: Who May Say What About Whom in Agentic Selection
items.dek: Standing—whether a publisher is entitled to assert about a competitor—is missing from twelve agent selection defenses.
items.unproven: theoretical framework only; no empirical implementation; no measurement of standing-aware filtering on real agents; applicability to SDLC tooling unclear.

items.title: The Maximum Nonlinearity of 8-variable Balanced Boolean Functions is 116
items.dek: Maximum nonlinearity of 8-variable balanced Boolean functions proven to be 116, resolving Dobbertin's conjecture.

items.title: Same Attack, Different Judge: A First Controlled Adversarial Comparison of Jev, LLM Judges, and Purpose-Built Safety Classifiers
items.dek: Jev structured-query safety judge outperforms LLM judges on input moderation but underperforms on phishing at 62% vs 77-81%.
items.unproven: narrow task scope (four tasks); commercial product; vendor makes the system being evaluated; generalization to reader's own SAST/DAST rule-tuning workflows unclear.

items.title: SkillScreen: High-Recall Screening of Malicious Agent Skills with Decision Models
items.dek: SkillScreen decision model flags 20-25% of benign agent skills at 99% recall; generalizes better than fine-tuned encoders to unseen attacks.
items.unproven: trained only on MaliciousSkillBench; unfamiliar benign sources sharply increase false positives; unclear if applicable to SDLC-integrated agent screening pipelines.

items.title: BrowseSafe++: Benchmarking Prompt Injection Detection Across Web Contexts, Languages, and Browser Views
items.dek: BrowseSafe++ expands prompt-injection benchmark to 38,675 page pairs with 24 attack types and trains 0.8B detectors outperforming frontier models.
items.unproven: whether 0.8B detectors catch injection variants beyond the 24 types and 18 locations represented; generalization to zero-day payload shapes

items.title: VeriRouter: Towards Verifiable LLM Routing
items.dek: VeriRouter uses ZK proofs and provider certificates to verify LLM router integrity without exposing routing logic.
items.unproven: whether proof latencies (21.92s, 4.24s) scale linearly with workload diversity; adoption in production routing systems

items.title: Rethinking Quality in Large Language Model Routing: Security-Conditioned Model-and-Budget Selection
items.dek: SCRouter balances utility and security in LLM routing by selecting model and token budget; 38,869-query benchmark across nine security dimensions.
items.unproven: Benchmark is synthetic; does not establish whether routing decisions prevent real attacks on production agents or apply to agents the reader's SDLC is instrumenting.

items.title: FedGraph: Defending Federated Large Language Model Fine-Tuning Against Backdoor Attacks via Graph-Based Aggregation
items.dek: Graph-based aggregation detects backdoored client updates in federated LLM fine-tuning by modeling consistency differences.
items.unproven: evaluated on synthetic backdoor scenarios; does not address adaptive attacks or federated SDLC workflows the reader owns

items.title: Holding Agents Accountable with Verifiable Agent Insurance
items.dek: Smart-contract escrow for agent misbehavior recovery; tested on three agent benchmarks.
items.unproven: requires blockchain infrastructure adoption; untested against sophisticated agents or adversarial providers; no evidence financial recovery matches actual harm.

items.title: ProtoArena: Can AI Agents Discover and Exploit Real-World Cross-Component Protocol Vulnerabilities?
items.dek: ProtoArena benchmark: LLM agents achieve 48.8% success on 80 protocol-exploitation tasks under guidance, 12.5% black-box.
items.unproven: narrow domain (protocol vulnerabilities); five LLM baseline only; unclear whether findings transfer to non-protocol attack surfaces; reader does not conduct agent red-teaming.

noise.title: Redesigning source control at Anthropic
noise.dek: Anthropic describes its internal source control architecture; applicable insights are organizational and tooling patterns, not technique.
noise.unproven: generalization beyond Anthropic's scale and deployment model; transferability to financial services SDLC unclear.

noise.title: Doory – Open-Source Canva
noise.dek: Open-source Canva clone; general software engineering project unrelated to security or SDLC.

noise.title: I Found a $90k Remote Code Execution Vulnerability in Google
noise.dek: $90k Google RCE writeup; single finding disclosed post-remediation, not actionable threat.
noise.unproven: vulnerability already patched; demonstrates no ongoing exposure to reader's environment
